summary: 1931 L-4 cab on Border Peak in Sanders County, listed under Lolo National Forest; one listing says destroyed in 1962, another says removed. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: One listing says destroyed in 1962; another lists the site only as removed, with no date.

events.note: L-4 cab; an October 7, 1931 newspaper item, as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, says lookout houses were being constructed at Border Peak
Listed as removed, with no date

evidence.supports: newspaper item of October 7, 1931 reporting Bob Paulin and Jim Carter building at Border Peak
evidence.quote: at Border Peak by Bob Paulin and Jim Carter

evidence.supports: site listed as removed, no date
state list marks the site as gone (ground-level structure)
L-4 cab was by far the most popular live-in lookout design
evidence.quote: L-4 cab was by far the most popular live-in lookout.

evidence.supports: L-4 cab described as a 14 by 14 foot wood-frame cab
evidence.quote: It was a 14x14' wood frame cab

evidence.supports: L-4 cab described with windows all around
evidence.quote: wood frame cab, windows all around

evidence.supports: lookout houses under construction when the item ran (work under way by October 1931)
evidence.quote: Lookout houses are now being constructed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says destroyed in 1962; the Forest Lookouts page lists it as removed with no date. Both are reported in the story; neither source gives the cause.

sources.title: Remember When: Lookouts in Sanders County

notes_for_editor: Brief record is consistent with sources: coordinates, Ground type and Lolo National Forest agency all match. Build year 1931 is supported by two sources. Fate conflicts (destroyed 1962 vs removed, undated). Nothing found on staffing, fires or current condition. Sanders County Ledger column (cite 4) is general on L-4 design and does not list Border Peak.
